legal.title: 📋 Legal notice & GDPR
legal.controller: Filenymous is open-source software. Files travel directly from one browser to the other (WebRTC) and are never stored by the publisher: there is no file database. Each user remains responsible for the files they share.
legal.data: To connect the two browsers, a signaling server temporarily exchanges the transfer code and network connection details (IP addresses, WebRTC parameters). When a direct connection is impossible, a TURN relay forwards the already-encrypted bytes (AES-256-GCM) without being able to read or keep them. Nothing is persisted. The browser and OS name (e.g. “Chrome · Windows”) is exchanged only between the two peers. No cookies, no ads; only anonymous audience measurement (see below).
legal.audience: We use Umami, an open-source analytics tool that we host ourselves (OVHcloud VPS in Europe, www.opendpe.net): no data is shared with third parties. It sets no cookie and stores nothing in your browser. For each page view it only receives the page path (e.g. “/app/”, never the part after “#” or “?”, so never your links, keys, codes or passwords), the address of the page you came from, without parameters or fragment, the language and screen size, and derives the browser, OS, device type and country/region from the request. Your IP address is used for that and for a hashed visit identifier renewed every day; it is not stored. Nothing is measured on the secret and whistleblowing (report) pages. If your browser sends “Do Not Track” or “Global Privacy Control”, nothing is sent. Legal basis: legitimate interest (aggregated visit statistics); you can also block www.opendpe.net/umami/ with a content blocker.
legal.erasure: Since nothing is stored on a server, there is nothing to erase on the publisher’s side: closing the sender’s tab ends the share and makes the link useless. The decryption key only exists inside the shared link.
legal.hosting: The site is hosted by OVHcloud (France). The signaling and TURN relay servers run on an OVHcloud VPS in Europe; they never see file contents.
legal.terms: Files are shared directly between browsers, with no server storage. Only send files you have the right to share, only share links with recipients you know, and do not use Filenymous for illegal or harmful content. By sending a file, you confirm that you understand and accept these terms.

privacy.title: Privacy: what is protected, and what is not
privacy.e2ee: Content (files, names, notes) is encrypted in the browser (AES-256-GCM). The key only exists in the link, after “#”, which browsers never send to the server.
privacy.ram: Nothing is stored on a server or in browser storage: content lives in the memory of the host's and participants' tabs and is wiped when the wall is destroyed, when the host leaves, or on close.
privacy.relay: The signaling relay never sees the key, the password, the wall name or the content: only an opaque wall id and WebRTC connection parameters. It keeps no access log for walls, but sees your IP address during the connection (in-memory rate limiting).
privacy.ip: This is not anonymity: with WebRTC, the host sees each participant's IP address and each participant sees the host's (unless a TURN relay is used).
privacy.tor: To hide your IP address, use a trusted VPN; Tor Browser disables WebRTC and cannot be used for the wall.
privacy.whistle: For a sensitive report (source, whistleblower), prefer the whistleblowing channel, which works with Tor Browser:
privacy.screens: Destroying the wall wipes in-memory copies, not what a participant already downloaded, copied or photographed.
privacy.live: Live streams (screen, camera, mic): only after you agree, relayed by the host's tab over encrypted WebRTC connections (DTLS-SRTP) negotiated inside the encrypted channel; the host sees the stream, the relay never does.
privacy.agents: AI agents: off by default. When the host allows them, everything an agent reads is sent to its AI model provider, outside end-to-end encryption. The “AI” badge is self-declared.

onb.title: Create your vault
onb.lead: A local-first vault: your secrets are encrypted in this browser before being saved, and only ever leave it encrypted, to the contacts you choose.

local.d: In this browser's private storage (encrypted SQLite), not on a server.

zero.d: Argon2id + AES-256-GCM. Without your password (or phrase), nobody can open it, not even us.

p2p.d: Encrypted, signed WebRTC (X25519 + Ed25519), straight to your contact's vault.

search.d: Local full-text search, plus optional semantic search with a small AI running in the tab.

onb.localWarn: Important: the vault lives in this browser. Clearing the site's data deletes it. Export an encrypted backup regularly (Settings).
onb.methodTitle: How do you want to unlock your vault?
onb.tooWeak: Too weak: aim for at least {{bits}} bits (4 to 5 random words work great).
onb.passwordHint: It is never sent or stored. Nobody can reset it: only your recovery phrase replaces it.
onb.passkeyLead: Your device (Touch ID, Windows Hello, a security key…) derives a secret key through the WebAuthn PRF extension. You can add a password later.
onb.kdf: Your password is stretched with Argon2id (64 MB of memory, 3 passes): it takes a second or two, and makes every guess expensive for an attacker.
onb.phraseLead: These 24 words reopen the vault if you forget your password. Click a word to reveal it and write them down in order, on paper, offline.
onb.noReset: There is no reset. Without your password or this phrase, the vault's content is lost for good. Don't photograph it or paste it into any online service.
onb.ack: I wrote down the 24 words, in order, offline
onb.ackHint: This phrase will never be shown again.
onb.checkLead: Type the requested words to confirm your copy is right.
onb.checkErr: One of the words doesn't match. Check your copy.

backup.title: Backup
backup.clearWarning: Clearing this site's browsing data (or uninstalling the browser) deletes the vault. Keep an up-to-date backup.
backup.explain: The backup is the vault file as is: only encrypted data and your wrapped keys. It reopens with your password or recovery phrase, in any browser.
backup.imported: Backup restored. Unlock it with its password or phrase.
backup.importLead: Choose a .fnyvault file exported from Filenymous. It will replace this browser's vault.
backup.replaceMsg: This browser's vault will be replaced by the backup.
backup.notPersisted: Storage not persistent (the browser may evict it when space runs low)
backup.persistNo: The browser declined (often granted once the site is installed or bookmarked).
backup.banner: Your vault only exists in this browser. Export an encrypted backup so nothing is lost if you clear your browsing data or change device.

privacy.title: How it's protected (and the limits)
privacy.local: The vault is a SQLite database in this browser's private storage (OPFS); only encrypted blobs are written to it (AES-256-GCM). The search index only exists in memory, while the vault is open.
privacy.keys: A random key encrypts the vault; it is wrapped by your password (Argon2id), your passkey (PRF) and your recovery phrase (BIP-39).
privacy.p2p: Shares travel over direct WebRTC; the signaling relay only sees an opaque inbox id and IP addresses, never the content.
privacy.rights: Roles and expiry are honoured by the recipient's Filenymous app, not guaranteed cryptographically.
privacy.memory: Locking wipes keys from memory on a best-effort basis; a compromised device (malware, malicious extension) can read everything while the vault is open.
privacy.storage: Clearing the site's data deletes the vault: export backups.

invite.linkHonest: This link and QR code only contain your public contact card (identifier {{handle}}), never your secrets. They only let the person add you as a contact. Send them over a channel you trust, then check the identifier together.
invite.incomingLead: Someone sent you their public contact card. Adding it lets you share vault items with them; it gives them access to nothing.
invite.verify: Check this identifier with the person (in person or over another channel) before sharing anything: anyone who handled this link could have changed it.
invite.replyLead: So this person can share items with you too, send them your own link back:
invite.self: This is your own contact card.
invite.pendingUnlock: A contact invite is waiting: create or unlock your vault to add it.

privacyPanel.keys: Encryption keys are generated in your browser and never leave it. No central authority issues identities.
privacyPanel.chunks: Files are split into chunks, each encrypted with AES-256-GCM before leaving your device.
privacyPanel.direct: Files go straight from one browser to the other (WebRTC). The signalling server only introduces the browsers; a TURN relay, if needed, only sees encrypted bytes.
privacyPanel.wall: On the sharing wall, the host's tab relays exchanges between participants over encrypted WebRTC connections. The signalling server has no access to them and nothing is stored on a server.
privacyPanel.stop: Closing the sender's tab ends the share: the link stops working.
privacyPanel.fragment: The decryption key sits after the “#” in the link: it is never sent to the server.
